s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with localized erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels with plump endothelial cells
positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34
key_facts: female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
lesions located on left upper arm, axilla, and lateral thoracic region
lesions are firm, nonscaly, and have irregular borders
no triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma
no fever, weight loss, or fatigue
histopathological examination shows thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels
endothelial cells are plump with no significant cytologic atypia
immunohistochemistry positive for CD31, CD34, and Ki-67 (<1%)
immunohistochemistry negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological findings of irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's skin lesions and histopathological examination showing thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: acquired tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical presentation of firm, nonscaly, erythematous patches and plaques, and histopathological findings of irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's localized cutaneous vascular lesions and histopathological examination showing irregularly branched blood vessels

shortlist.label: epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological findings of plump endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The patient's histopathological examination showing thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels with plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34, along with the clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, is consistent with retiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Negative immunohistochemistry for HHV-8 and lack of systemic symptoms or extracutaneous involvement

rejected.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and histopathological features do not match the characteristic targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition of this condition

rejected.label: acquired tufted angioma
rejected.why: Histopathological examination does not show the characteristic tufted or cannonball appearance of this condition

rejected.label: epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Lack of significant cytologic atypia and negative immunohistochemistry for podoplanin (D2-40) do not support this diagnosis
